relationships.subject: Nav1.8
relationships.evidence_quote: Nav1.8 subtraction resulted in a near-linear reduction of AP overshoot from 43.1 ± 2.7 mV (n = 13) in control to 28.3 ± 5.5 mV (n = 12) and 12.6 ± 6.8 mV (n = 12, P = 0.0012) after subtraction of 50% and 100% of Nav1.8 Gmax, respectively.

relationships.subject: Nav1.8
relationships.evidence_quote: We found a linear correlation (R2 = 0.96) between AP voltage threshold and level of Nav1.8 conductance change in the ±1.0 (0.25 to 0.5 increments) Nav1.8 Gmax range (Fig. 2C).

relationships.subject: Nav1.8
relationships.evidence_quote: Functional addition of Nav1.8 conductance not only decreased AP rheobase but also promoted repetitive AP firing.

relationships.subject: Nav1.8
relationships.evidence_quote: Supercharging the membrane with additional Nav1.8 conductance enhanced amplitude of the oscillations while Nav1.8 subtraction abolished oscillations

relationships.subject: Nav1.7L858H
relationships.evidence_quote: On average, induction of the Nav1.7WT/LH model reduced the rheobase of wild-type neurons by 34.3 ± 5.5% (n = 19)

key_findings: Dynamic clamp showed Nav1.8 conductance linearly sets AP voltage threshold and overshoot, with no effect on undershoot or resting potential.

DRG neurons split into strong (~50%) and weak responders to Nav1.8 subtraction; in Nav1.7L858H neurons, 50% Nav1.8 subtraction restored rheobase in strong responders (63%) but weak responders (37%) stayed hyperexcitable.
